PUBLICATION_CALL_REPORTED_FAILURE_WHILE_: One batched osascript call publishing P072-P076 returned an ERROR to the coordinating session but had RUN TO COMPLETION: all five repositories created (timestamps 11:12:28 to 11:12:59) and all five pushed. The error came from the shell function's return status, not the work. The session then retried P072 believing it had failed; the retry built a second local copy with a fresh git history and its push was CORRECTLY REFUSED as a non-fast-forward, so nothing was clobbered - but only because git refused, not because the retry was safe. Diagnosed by querying each repository's pushed_at, default branch and remote SHA before touching anything, rather than trusting either the error or the earlier existence check. GENERAL LESSON: through this bridge a non-zero exit status does NOT mean the work did not happen. Verify remote state before retrying a publication step.
PULP_CARRY_OVER_CLOSED_PREMISE_WAS_WRONG: The open question - do published P004, P023, P032 still pass with no PuLP solver present - is answered, and the premise was wrong. pulp 3.3.2 DOES ship an available bundled solver: listSolvers(onlyAvailable=True) returns ['PULP_CBC_CMD']. The solver only disappears at pulp 4: at 4.1.0 and 4.2.0 that call returns [] and PULP_CBC_CMD is not in listSolvers() at all. Measured by running each product's own suite. Under its DECLARED pin: P004 (pulp>=2.7,<4 -> 3.3.2) 106/106 PASS with 218 PULP_CBC_CMD deprecation warnings; P023 (pulp>=3,<4 -> 3.3.2) 185/185 PASS; P032 (pulp>=3 unbounded -> 4.2.0) 387/387 PASS. Under the container's system pulp 4.2.0, outside P004's and P023's declared range: P004 17 of 106 FAIL with TypeError LpVariable.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'cat'; P023 1 of 185 FAIL with AttributeError on pulp.PULP_CBC_CMD; P032 387/387 PASS because it calls pulp_solver_available(), sees the empty list and falls back to scipy. CONCLUSION: no published product is broken as declared. The failures are pulp 4 API BREAKS, not solver absence, and P004 and P023 are protected precisely by the <4 ceiling the mission's own bounded-on-both-sides rule required. TWO CONSEQUENCES: P032's pulp>=3 is unbounded above, violates that rule, and passes only by runtime detection - it needs a ceiling; and P004/P023 are on a deprecation countdown, using an API pulp 3.3.2 warns about 218 times and pulp 4 removed.

NEW_DEFECT_CLASS_SUBPROCESS_ENV_POLLUTES: A build can pollute its own tree through a subprocess environment it sets itself. P074's own validate_cli.py started subprocesses with HOME set to the product root, so matplotlib wrote .config/matplotlib INTO the repository, which would have tripped gate checks 8 and 9. Fixed with a temporary HOME and MPLCONFIGDIR plus PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, and the same hygiene applied to the two other scripts that spawn subprocesses. Added to the build guide.
